clues: This city sits where two rivers join, near the middle of its state. It grew where the two streams meet and flow on as one.
Snow stays light here, since this city sits too far from the great lakes for their big lake snows. Yet those lakes still send long grey cloudy spells in winter.
The state's chiefs kept moving the capital from town to town. So in 1812 they built a new city in the centre and made it the capital in 1816.
Just north of town, a zoo on the river banks is famed round the world, thanks to its director Jack Hanna. A top guide once named it the best zoo in the land.
The lawmakers of Ohio meet in this city, in the statehouse built on a square set aside for it. From here they run the whole state.
